answer: An observatory selling ridge surveys and mirror-alignment readings issues a random challenge at solar zenith. Each voting slot must prove it holds a separately encoded 1 GB replica committed a day earlier, then return unpredictable sampled blocks before a short deadline. A proof-of-replication scheme binds each replica to its slot; epoch-bound challenges prevent replay. Extra aliases thus need extra storage and ongoing responses, rather than just new keys. The cost is storage and bandwidth; well-funded farms remain possible.
